refuted_claims:
1. Panel-design cost and yield (section 4.6, verdict point 6, recommendations 4 and 7). The explorer's claims were "4.9x the cells", "about 2.7x the solver tokens", "+56M", "movers per 1,000 cells fall from 11.4 to 9.1", and "only the scope-filtered designs raise the yield (13.2)".
   - Its model (analyse_r2.py line 116; designs: items x 6 arms x TRIGGER_RUNS, summed per rule) charges the 4 placebo controls once per rule. In v3 the controls run once on the union of a stage's trigger items. The model also re-counts the first GATE_RUNS runs of the rule and parent, which the focal panel already pays for.
   - My incremental model (sum of trigger sets x (T-G), plus union x (T-G) for the parent, plus union x T x 4 for the controls) reproduces the actual screen cell counts exactly: I-ds s1 1,200+400+322 = 1,922 and E-ds s1 1,600+400+510 = 2,510.
   - Under it, v3 trigger costs 2,078 cells and v4 all-in-scope 7,472, i.e. 3.6x, not 4.9x. Tokens are 26.2M vs 60.1M, i.e. 2.3x and +34M, not 2.7x and +56M. This uses all-cell token means.
   - Movers per 1,000 incremental cells: v3 15.9, v4 17.3, scope-filtered 16.6, in-scope failures 16.9, whole check half 22.7. The "lower yield" of v4 and the "higher yield" of scope-filtering are artifacts of the cell model. The +34M is still a real cost (about +24% of a 139M run).
2. The scope-filtered trigger recommendation.
   - It saves only 8% of incremental tokens (26.2M to 24.2M) and loses 9/33 two-run movers and 6/22 up items. C1 is already starved of power.
   - It pushes 4 of the 15 screened rules below MIN_TRIGGER = 4 (I-ds s1-r1 3, I-ds s1-r4 1, E-ds s1-r3 1, E-ds s1-r4 2). They would become insufficient_support. I-ds s1-r1 is the only rule whose effect is localized. The report does not mention this.
3. The claims "Rules do not act more where their condition holds" and "refutes all three premises".
   - The pooled discordance replicates: 98/505 vs 76/402, my permutation p = 0.596. But the statistic ignores direction, and the net test was one-sided for benefit only.
   - In the I-ds chain (task-card seed, the owner's yardstick) net harm concentrates in scope: 10 up / 21 down in scope (sign p = 0.071) vs 11/8 out of scope; stratified net permutation, one-sided p = 0.006. This is post hoc, one of about 7 splits I tried, so about 0.04 after Bonferroni. E-ds: p = 0.91.
   - With no rule showing a detectable effect anywhere, premise 3 is untestable on v3 data, not refuted. The report itself says "a scope filter cannot concentrate a signal that is not there".
4. verdict_cn "与人工判断一致的约占89%" (agreement with human judgment about 89%). All 180 reference labels are LLM-agent labels:
   - 60 are the r2 explorer's own, and it also wrote the conditions;
   - 120 are the first-attempt explorer's (its report calls them "a careful human reading"), written against different condition wording.
   - No human labelled anything.
5. Transfer of the judge reliability and cost figures to v4/v5. They were measured at temperature 0 on question-only fields, at 408-1,151 tokens per call.
   - The v4 spec P1/P4 (docs/handoff/v4-plans-20261021/spec.md lines 129-152) votes at ROLE_VOTE_TEMPERATURE = 0.7. It shows "the task card + the item's public text, exactly as the examiner sees it" (ROLE_INPUT_BYTES 220,000).
   - So the 87% unanimity, the 85% vagueness flag, "2+1 = about 2.1 calls" and "2.2M per chain" are not established for the configuration that will actually run. With solver-size inputs (2.4k-5.6k tokens per item) the judge cost is plausibly about 5x, around 10M per chain [E].
6. Minor points:
   - The "always in disguise" list includes I-ds s3-r2 at 42/49 (86%), below the report's own 90% threshold.
   - "Fewer runs on FF items" as the dead-item lever contradicts its own table: FF items hold 14 of the 22 up items.
confirmed_claims:
Independent recount from the frozen v3 cells (training, screen and confirm paths only):
- 49 proposals: 28 supported, 8 evidence_invalid, 8 insufficient_support, 2 dropped_pre_dispatch, 1 invalid, 2 leak.
- 15 screen arms: 13 fail, 2 pass (I-ds s4-r2, E-ds s1-r1). The context's "14 screened" is wrong. 2 confirm arms, both fail.
- 143 trigger items; 71 strict-dead (72 when the one cell with an unknown verdict counts); 22 up / 19 down at the trigger runs.

Other numbers checked:
- Per-cell token means (all cells), within about 7% of the explorer's 600-file sample: SearchQA 2,437 / OfficeQA 5,574 / LiveMath 2,930 / SpreadsheetBench 3,913 / ALFWorld 138,587, against 2,603 / 5,626 / 3,043 / 3,820 / 141,157.
- Pooled in-scope vs out-of-scope: 98/505 vs 76/402, net -2.5 vs +2.5.
- I-ds s1-r1 Fisher p = 0.0078.
- "First attempt's judge 110/120" is the majority of its three reason-then-label votes. Its report's 113/120 included a label-only vote.

Precision near the base rate holds:
- Stratified Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio 1.32 (p = 0.097) excluding the definitional LiveMath meta rows.
- Judged conditions only: 1.27 (p = 0.23). Screened judged only: 1.08 (p = 0.83).
- The median lift of 1.02 hides a weak positive tilt but not a usable classifier.

Dead items are not separable before solving. Logically, any probe without the rule arm cannot tell "nothing fixes it" from "only the rule fixes it".

E-ds s1-r1 non-replication, confirmed with independent cal-1 data (4 runs, 200 SearchQA training items):
- Check half: net -2.4 / -1.9 vs parent A / B; the v3 screen showed +4.5.
- Proposal half without evidence: -5.3 / -7.1; the explorer found -7.0.
- Its own 8 evidence items: +2.25, 4 up / 0 down. It fits its evidence and harms elsewhere.
- No in-scope concentration: 25/66 moved (net -0.4) vs 11/33 (net -2.0).

v4 design and C1 threshold:
- The v4 spec P1 does set trigger = all check-half items judged applicable, with "same runs, same thresholds, same controls".
- So the warning that a fixed "gain >= 1 whole item" threshold gets easier to pass as the panel grows (null pass of the gain part 0.26 -> 0.36) is sound in direction.

Literature:
- AutoGuide: NeurIPS 2024 main track; arXiv 2403.08978; authors correct.
- Its full text confirms that selection precision is never measured. Appendix A: "there lacks a standardized method for quantifying the quality of generated contexts and selected guidelines".
- Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990, J Clin Epidemiol 43:543-549, and Fleiss 1971, Psychol Bull 76(5):378-382, are both correct.

missing:
1. Positive control. The context flags cal-1 as usable now, but the report never uses it.
   - The one real effect, task card vs empty scaffold (46 up / 13 down over 200 items), is not concentrated in any of the six SearchQA conditions. For "minimal name" it is +0.053 per item in scope vs +0.174 out of scope. Task-feature conditions do not mark where text effects land, even for a real effect.
   - Placebo texts move 12-37 of 99 items (control:3 is 8 up / 29 down) against 20/99 for same-text noise. A diagnostic built on movement rates (the explorer's recommended scope-specificity flag) cannot separate a real effect from a perturbation. It must use direction.
2. Conditional injection, the literature's actual use of conditions.
   - AutoGuide identifies context per step from the trajectory ("At each timestep, AutoGuide identifies the context of the current test trajectory"), i.e. runtime conditions, which D4 sets aside. It injects only the matching guidelines. Its WebShop ablation: guidelines without contexts 37% vs AutoGuide 46%.
   - Used as an injection gate, a predicate makes the rule arm identical to the parent on out-of-scope items. That removes the measured 18.9% out-of-scope perturbation by construction, makes C2/C3/C4' on non-applicable items free (cells can be shared), and gives a transfer mechanism: the rule applies where its condition holds on the similar benchmark and stays silent on dissimilar ones.
   - Untested. It costs one judge call per item per rule at solve time and changes the "Skill = plain text" format.
3. Owner constraints.
   - No analysis of transfer to similar benchmarks (C4'), although a when-predicate naturally defines the similar-target panel.
   - No split by chain. The largest effects (E-ds s1-r1/r2) are measured against an empty scaffold, which the owner rejects as the yardstick, and the I-ds chain behaves differently (point 3 of the refutations).
4. Power. There is no true-positive (power) calculation per design. Designs are ranked only on null pass and movers per cell, and movers are mostly noise.
5. The evidence-coverage gate's benefit is unmeasured.
   - Conditions already cover their own evidence at 79% (126/159 against 55% by chance). Check-half recall enrichment is only 1.18 (169/284 vs a 50.5% match rate, LiveMath meta rows excluded).
   - The rules look fitted to their evidence. Enforcing coverage may tighten that fit rather than improve generalization.
6. Not addressed:
   - the 3 runtime rules and the ALFWorld cost (about 138.6k tokens per cell, 74% of the v3 trigger tokens);
   - the interaction with MIN_TRIGGER.
notes_cn: 结论：主要否定结论站得住，但有几处要更正。我独立复核了流程计数（49条规则、15条进检验、0条通过、71道死题），都正确；4轮校准数据也证实那条初筛通过的规则只是波动。需要更正的有：一、成本算法重复计算了共用的对照组，第四版方案实际多花约2.3倍而非2.7倍，单位花费的信息量也不比原方案低；二、它推荐的过滤方案会让4条规则因不足4道题而无法检验；三、在用任务说明起步的那条链上，规则造成的退步集中在“适用”的题里（事后检验），所以“规则不在适用题上起作用”说过头了；四、“人工判断”其实是模型自己的标注。它还漏掉了“只在条件成立时才放入规则”的用法，也没讨论向相似基准的迁移。
